headline: Ten Thousand Islands Waterway and Gulf Access
reservation: Wilderness permits are required for all overnight backcountry camping in the nearby national park waters, managed via a central reservation system. Day-use boat tours and rentals are separate commercial entities and should be booked well in advance during the dry season. Verify the specific launch site as some locations are tide-dependent and require official check-in.

days.title: Mangrove Tunnels and Coastal Keys
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Gulf Coast Visitor Center

stops.name: Ten Thousand Islands National Wildlife Refuge
stops.detail: Navigate the labyrinth of mangroves to spot manatees and migratory birds in their natural estuary.

stops.name: Smallwood Store
stops.detail: Step into a preserved 1906 trading post that served as the primary link for early settlers on Chokoloskee Island.

days.driving: Local travel by boat; allow 3–5 hours depending on tide cycles
days.note: Tidal movements are significant; local charts must be consulted for all water-based transit.

days.title: Big Cypress Vistas and Swamp Boardwalks

stops.name: Big Cypress National Preserve
stops.detail: Drive the Loop Road for sightings of alligators and cypress knees in the freshwater marl prairies.

stops.name: Clyde Butcher’s Big Cypress Gallery
stops.detail: View large-format wilderness photography and walk the surrounding nature path through the swamp.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the slow-speed scenic loop; conditions vary with water levels
days.note: Portions of the scenic loop are unpaved; check vehicle clearance and weather impacts.

days.title: Historic Town and River Exploration

stops.name: Everglades City Hall
stops.detail: Admire the historic Neoclassical architecture of the former Collier County Courthouse.

stops.name: Turner River
stops.detail: Launch a kayak to experience the transition from sawgrass prairies to dense mangrove canopies.

days.driving: Minimal driving; primary transit is via paddle or small vessel
days.note: Biting insects are prevalent year-round; plan for higher activity in shaded mangrove areas.

intel.title: Public Boat Ramp Access
intel.text: The Everglades City public ramp fills early during fishing tournaments. Limited street parking is available for oversized trailers near the circle.

intel.title: Waterway Dead Zones
intel.text: Cellular coverage is non-existent once deep in the mangrove islands. Carry a physical nautical chart and a VHF radio for emergency communication.

intel.title: Marine and Road Supply
intel.text: On-water fuel is available at select marinas in Everglades City and Chokoloskee. Ensure land vehicles are fueled in Naples before entering the rural glades corridors.

intel.title: Tide Window Constraints
intel.text: Many mangrove tunnels become impassable at low tide, while high tide can limit clearance under bridges. Consult NOAA tide tables for the Barron River station.

intel.title: Backcountry Permits
intel.text: Access to remote chickees and keys for overnight stays requires a physical permit printout. Check the Recreation.gov window for seasonal availability.

plan.arrival: Land at RSW, drive 90 minutes south via I-75 and SR-29, and secure watercraft rentals before afternoon breezes pick up.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance vehicles are recommended for unpaved preserve roads; standard cars are fine for the town and main highways.
plan.goldenHour: Chokoloskee Island bridge provides a panoramic westward view over the Ten Thousand Islands for sunset photography.
